notes:
Account snapshot: Glint CrossCorpus is a pan-European legal analytics platform building a single-search surface across multilingual corpora (contracts, court opinions, regulatory filings). POC goal: replace current Elastic+manual reranker stack with Redwood serving embed+rerank pipeline to cut median latency and cost per query while improving per-language recall.

Highlights / ask:
- Corpus size: ~12M documents (~45M passages after chunking). Expect steady-state indexing growth 10-15% qtr.
- Languages of priority: EN, FR, DE, ES, NL, PT, IT, PL, JA. Rising interest in JA and PL where recall lags.
- Workload: 6k peak qps (search requests), typical concurrency 250-600 qps; heavy tail for long context legal queries.
- Indexing approach: embeddings at paragraph level (~1536-d) + dense vector index; candidate generation ~100 per query, neural reranker to top-20.
- Perf targets: p50 end-to-end <120ms, p95 <350ms (user-facing). Currently p95 ~420ms on baseline (Elastic + external reranker).
- Cost targets: target < $0.004/query (embeddings+rerank); current POC run estimates $0.007/query without batching/CACHE. Cost sensitivity high.
- Quality targets: per-language recall@10: EN 0.92 target, FR 0.87 target, DE 0.88 target, JA 0.78 target. Current POC recall by lang: EN 0.91, FR 0.83, DE 0.86, JA 0.72, PL 0.69. Need per-language tuning.
- Reranker notes: using Transformer-based cross-encoder for top-20 re-rank; heavy CPU/GPU consideration for latency. Exploring quantized reranker on dedicated GPU pools and batched rerank windows to shave cost.
- Multilingual pain points: tokenizer mismatch for CJK languages, stopword handling affecting recall on legal short queries, cross-lingual embeddings quality varies by model and available fine-tuning data.
- Routing: interest in model-routing by language (fast L2 for EN/DE/FR, fallback cross-lingual model for low-resource languages). Also want automatic fallback to cheaper model for non-critical queries.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-09-18: Lead created after inbound webinar download. AE assigned (Priya).
- 2025-09-30: Discovery call — high-level requirements, security questionnaire requested.
- 2025-10-14: POC kickoff — ingest sample 1.2M docs (FF id attached).
- 2025-10-28: Indexing job completed for core EU corpus; initial embed vectors stored. Benchmarks v1 run.
- 2025-11-01: Live demo — Redwood hosted+dedicated comparison. Reranker integrated; observed p95 improvement but still above target. (FF-20251101-GLINT).
- 2025-11-04: Security review draft feedback received; asks for KMS attestations and EU-residency SLA language.

Quotes / snippets from stakeholders:
- "We need comparable or better recall in Japanese and Polish — those are deal-breakers for litigation teams." — Head of Search (email 2025-10-27)
- "If you can get p95 under 350ms and show cost reduction, we can move to procurement Q1." — CTO (call 2025-11-01)

Technical POC notes / asks for Redwood team:
- Provide recommended model/quantization profile for embeddings (multilingual 1536-d candidate) and a small/medium cross-encoder for rerank with latency-cost tradeoffs.
- Suggest batching & prefix-KV cache settings for common query patterns.
- Trial routing policy examples: language-based primary+fallback model map; cost-tier fallback for non-sensitive queries.
- Provide per-language evaluation harness (precision/recall by lang + confusion matrix) and recommended eval prompt sets.
- Need an EU-residency option for private deployment or dedicated pools in eu-west region.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood SE (Diego) to run perf pass with quantized reranker on dedicated GPU pool (week of 2025-11-10).
- Deliver per-language eval report (EN/FR/DE/ES/JA/PL) and proposed model map.
- Legal to receive KMS and residency SOW (drive link).

Sticking points / blockers:
- Legal needs formal data residency proof and KMS/HSM integration detail.
- JA/PL recall gaps require additional labeled data or specialist fine-tuning; customer evaluating cost/benefit.
- Final budget owner (Procurement) not in demo calls yet.
